key_insight: A DSL-guided multi-agent LLM system can improve inverse materials design by grounding natural-language design rules in symbolic predicates and statistical evidence.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a low-training, interpretable path to search for candidate perovskite oxides under multiple target-property constraints, which is useful for computational materials engineering workflows.
method: Translate natural-language design rules into chemistry DSL predicates.
Use accumulated materials data to test, refine, and validate rules during iterative LLM design loops.
Deploy a multi-agent framework (ORCHESTRA) for inverse design of double perovskite oxides.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that DSL-grounded symbolic predicates helped identify unsupported rules, validate new ones, and improve performance compared with a natural-language-only strategy, especially for harder target properties.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the underlying materials data and DSL rules, so incomplete rule encoding could limit generalization.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
